Apple announced today that its new M4 chip will feature a dedicated Neural Engine capable of 38 trillion operations per second, a significant leap from the M3's 18 TOPS. The chip will debut in the new iPad Pro lineup and later in MacBook Air models. Apple emphasized that the increased NPU performance enables on-device AI inference without compromising battery life, a key differentiator from competitors that rely on cloud-based AI.

Summarize this product review in one sentence:

I've been using these wireless earbuds for about three months now. The sound quality is impressive for the price point, with clear highs and decent bass. Battery life is around 6 hours on a single charge, which is adequate but not outstanding. The fit is comfortable for extended use, though they can feel a bit loose during vigorous exercise. The noise cancellation works well in office environments but struggles with loud traffic. Overall, a solid mid-range option.

Summarize this technical documentation in 2-3 sentences:

The authentication system uses OAuth 2.0 with PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) for all client applications. Access tokens have a 15-minute lifetime and are automatically refreshed using the refresh token, which expires after 30 days. Token revocation is handled through a Redis-backed blacklist that is checked on every request. Rate limiting is applied at 100 requests per minute per user, with burst capacity of 150 requests.

Dear Team,

I hope this message finds you well. I wanted to provide an update on the server migration project. We have successfully completed the first phase, which involved moving all static assets to the new CDN. The second phase, database migration, is scheduled for this weekend starting Saturday at 2 AM UTC. During this time, there will be a planned downtime of approximately 4 hours. Please ensure all critical jobs are paused before the maintenance window. If you have any concerns, please reach out to the infrastructure team before Friday EOD.

Best regards,
Alex
